title: Insert Into
description:
Unlike eveything previous, there isn't really anything fancy, or special quirks to `INSERT INTO`.
```sql
-- INSERT INTO syntax:
INSERT INTO table_name (order_you_are_inserting_values_to_table) VALUES (values_in_order_defined_previously),(more_values(optional))....;
-- Let's say we have a table users with keys id, name, and age (INT TEXT INT). We can insert 3 values into this table like this: (note that the order you say how you insert the values can be in any order)
INSERT INTO users (name, id, age) VALUES ('steve', 12321, 21), ('bob', 99999, 18), ('alice', 1, 111);
-- Or you could insert one value like:
INSERT INTO users (id, name, age) VALUES (1, 'bill', 17);
```
---
# Assignment:
BWS wants you to add their 3 default versions to the instances map you made last time (it is still defined.). Insert into the instances table 3 instances with id 1 2 and 3, names 'BWS-V3', 'Server', and 'Blob storage', and give them all status 'running' and uptime 0.0.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE instances (id INT, name TEXT, status TEXT, uptime FLOAT);
runHarness: SELECT * FROM instances ORDER BY id asc;
expectedOutput:
id | name | status | uptime
1 | BWS-V3 | running | 0
2 | Server | running | 0
3 | Blob storage | running | 0
